people.name: Namkhai Norbu
people.field: Tibetan and Mongolian language and literature

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.role: Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Language and Literature
relations.evidence: served as Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Language and Literature from 1964 to 1992 at Naples Eastern University.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.role: taught the Tibetan language and literature
relations.evidence: In 1962, he took up a post in Naples at the Istituto Universitario Orientale, where he taught the Tibetan language and literature until 1992.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.object: Institute for the Middle and Far East (IsMEO)
relations.evidence: Norbu was invited to Italy by Giuseppe Tucci to work at the Institute for the Middle and Far East (IsMEO) in Rome for two years.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.evidence: He collaborated with Tucci and Geshe Jempel Senghe on a catalogue and library of Tibetan texts.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.evidence: He collaborated with Tucci and Geshe Jempel Senghe on a catalogue and library of Tibetan texts.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.evidence: At the age of sixteen, he met master Rigdzin Changchub Dorje (1863–1963), who became his main Dzogchen teacher.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.evidence: At the age of nine, he entered a Sakya college, where he studied Buddhist philosophy for many years with Khyenrab Chökyi Odzer.

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.evidence: In 1951, he received various teachings from the female yogi Ayu Khandro Dorje Paldrön (1838–1953).

relations.subject: Namkhai Norbu
relations.object: International Shang-Shung Institute for Tibetan Studies
relations.evidence: he founded the International Shang-Shung Institute for Tibetan Studies in 1990 to preserve the cultural traditions of Tibet

relations.subject: Adriano Clemente
relations.evidence: In 2002, Norbu oversaw the establishment of the Ka-Ter translation project, which tasked experienced translators such as Adriano Clemente, Elio Guarisco, and Jim Valby with the translation from Tibetan of key texts, as well as the works of Norbu himself.
